apps.name: CubeBrowser
apps.author: Arial-Bold
apps.short: Web browser with HTTPS, downloads and MIDI music
apps.long: A web browser for the GameCube. It loads websites over the Broadband Adapter, including secure (HTTPS) sites, with pictures, page styles, tables and forms. Files can be downloaded straight to the SD card, MIDI music plays in the background, and a Game Boy Advance on the link cable can act as the music player's screen and remote. Needs a network adapter. Settings, bookmarks and saved logins live in the gcbrowser folder and are kept on update.

apps.name: Snes9x GX
apps.author: dborth and contributors
apps.long: A Super Nintendo / Super Famicom emulator built on Snes9x, with a full menu for loading games, saving state and mapping controls. Put your ROMs (.smc, .sfc, or zipped) in sd:/snes9xgx/roms; save and settings folders are created on first use.

apps.name: FCE Ultra GX
apps.author: dborth and contributors
apps.short: NES / Famicom emulator with Famicom Disk System support
apps.long: An NES / Famicom emulator built on FCE Ultra, with a full menu for loading games, saving state and mapping controls. Put your ROMs (.nes, .fds, .unf, .nsf, or zipped) in sd:/fceugx/roms; disksys.rom for Famicom Disk System games goes in sd:/fceugx.

apps.name: GCMM
apps.author: suloku
apps.short: Memory card manager: back up and restore saves
apps.long: GameCube Memory Manager copies saves between the memory cards and the SD card: back up a whole card or single saves, restore them, delete saves, and fix or format a card. Backups go to the SD card.

apps.name: gcradio
apps.author: RyoSaeba89
apps.short: Internet radio: Icecast/SHOUTcast MP3, AAC and Opus
apps.long: Plays Icecast and SHOUTcast internet radio streams (MP3, AAC, Opus) over the Broadband Adapter, with a spectrum analyser. Starts on a default station; type another stream address on the console and it is remembered. This is the GX interface build. HTTPS stations need gcradio-ca.pem in sd:/apps/gcradio (see the homepage); plain HTTP streams work without it.

apps.name: Flashcube
apps.author: Arial-Bold
apps.short: Photo viewer with albums, slideshows and favourites
apps.long: Browse the photos on your SD card as a grid of thumbnails, by year, folder or favourites, with slideshows set to MIDI music and doodles saved as new photos. Photos go in sd:/DCIM as a camera stores them; songs for slideshows go in sd:/midi. Settings, favourites and thumbnails live in the app's folder and are kept on update.

apps.name: CubeVerse
apps.author: Arial-Bold
apps.long: Read and post in Juxtaposition communities, Pretendo Network's Miiverse revival: give Yeahs, comment, draw and follow people. Needs a network adapter and a Pretendo Network ID. Unofficial; not made or supported by Pretendo Network. Settings, your sign-in and the picture cache live in the app's folder and are kept on update.

apps.name: GC Station
apps.author: antho13otz
apps.short: Media centre: music, web radio, photos, podcasts (French)
apps.long: A media centre (formerly GC-MP3): music from sd:/mp3 (MP3, FLAC, OGG, AAC) with covers, lyrics and an equaliser, web radio, podcasts, photos and videos, a file browser, weather and news, and a phone remote over the Broadband Adapter. The interface is in French. Settings live in sd:/gc-mp3.

apps.name: Swiss
apps.author: emu_kidid and contributors
apps.short: Loader and multitool: games, homebrew, memory cards
apps.long: The GameCube loader: boots games and homebrew from SD, GC Loader, FlippyDrive, network and more, with game patches, video modes, cheats and memory card tools. Installs to sd:/apps/swiss. If your console boots Swiss from sd:/ipl.dol (PicoBoot or PicoLoader with gekkoboot), the browser offers to replace that too, along with sd:/swiss/patches/apploader.img if you have one (used by Apploader in-game reset), and moves the old ones to sd:/swiss_archive. Other boot methods (FlippyDrive, GC Loader, memory card, disc) keep their copy elsewhere; update those by hand from the homepage.

apps.name: Indigo
apps.author: spencernorton
apps.short: Fork of Swiss with a new interface: animated cube Home, poster library
apps.long: An unofficial fork of Swiss with the interface rebuilt: an animated glass cube for Home, a poster library and game details, and menu music. Device support, game patches and the loader are Swiss's own. Installs to sd:/apps/indigo and leaves your boot files alone. To start it when the console switches on, to get In-Game Reset back to it, or to use its Web face, copy the files by hand as its install guide says (norvitech.com/indigo/guide/install). Games go in sd:/games.

apps.name: Swiss 3D (fork)
apps.author: portlandhodl
apps.short: Fork of Swiss with a 3D interface, cover flow and network streaming
apps.long: An unofficial fork of Swiss rebuilt in 3D: glass cubes on the home menu, jewel cases and cover flow for games, a 3D file browser, menu sounds, screenshots and screen recording, and its own protocol for loading games over the Broadband Adapter. Everything else works as in Swiss. Installs to sd:/apps/swiss-3d, separate from Swiss, and leaves your boot files alone. To start it when the console switches on, copy it by hand from the homepage's release.

apps.name: Cube Menu
apps.author: hudsonbrendon
apps.short: Game menu with a 3D shelf of cases, clips and themes; games start through Swiss
apps.long: A game menu: a 3D shelf of game cases, gameplay clips and themes, details, play time, memory card backups and a launch scene. Games start through Swiss, so it needs Swiss's boot.dol at sd:/swiss/boot.dol (the Swiss in sd:/apps is not looked at), and games in sd:/games/<Name>/game.iso. Covers, clips and music come from cube-card, a tool you run on a computer; see the homepage. Without them it still lists your games, with blank cases.

apps.name: DOOM GC
apps.author: fromdustz
apps.short: Port of id Software's DOOM source. Bring your own WAD file
apps.long: id Software's 1997 DOOM source ported to the GameCube, with saving, a settings menu for controls, brightness and screen mode (Z on the main menu), and LAN play over the Broadband Adapter, which its author has not tested yet. No game data is included: installing creates sd:/doom, and you put your own WAD file there from a computer, next to doom.cfg. Any DOOM WAD should work; the author has tested version 1.9. Settings and saves live in sd:/doom and stay when the app is removed. If you already have an sd:/doom/doom.cfg it is left as it is.

apps.name: GC Homebrew Hub Browser
apps.author: GC Homebrew Hub
apps.short: This app store: browse, install, update and remove homebrew
apps.long: The program you are using. It lists the homebrew in its catalogs and installs, updates, starts and removes apps on the SD card, over the Broadband Adapter. An update puts the new files over the old ones in its folder; settings, sources and the log are kept. Start it again afterwards to run the new version.
